items.note: Master's thesis: 407 undergraduates did a restaurant-concept ideation and evaluation task under varying GenAI conditions, then were regrouped by actual behavior (no AI, AI-generated, augmented, prompt engineering); fluency, quality, and originality scored. Analysis groups are behavioral, not assigned, so check whether the original assigned-condition contrast is reported.

Turkish-language pretest-posttest quasi-experiment with 60 third-graders (30 vs 30): six weeks of ChatGPT-supported feedback on creative writing versus writing without feedback, scored on a creative-writing product scale; class-level non-random assignment.

HICSS paper: randomized experiment in which groups did collaborative ideation with humans only or with an AI collaborator suggesting ideas (plus an LLM idea editor for anonymity); participants' idea innovativeness scored. N not in abstract; same research group as c823, check for sample overlap.

ICIS paper: randomized 2x2 experiment (N=96) crossing idea-sharing structure with presence of an LLM AI peer in collaborative divergent thinking; fluency, elaboration, and originality scored. Abstract found through OpenAlex title search (no DOI); possible sample overlap with c822 (same authors).

Carleton HCI thesis: participants sketched websites with AI-generated inspiration, search-engine inspiration, or none; design performance and fixation scored on sketches. Assignment and N not in abstract; likely the same project as c825 (same author).

Nonprofessionals made wireframe prototypes with or without AI-generated sample designs; quality, accuracy, time, and user experience compared, moderated by visual imagery vividness. Abstract gives no N (search notes say 40, which would fall below 50); likely overlaps with the c824 thesis.

System paper (KidPrompt, a text-to-image tool for children) with a comparative study of 12 children on idea exploration and refinement; comparison condition and output scoring unclear, possibly system_paper_no_comparison or process-only measures; far below 50.

SSRN paper on frontloading manual sketching before generative AI versus AI-led design ideation, with design quality and idea variance outcomes per the search notes; abstract not reachable (SSRN 403, no OpenAlex/S2/Crossref abstract, APIs rate-limited), so design, N, and assignment are unconfirmed.
IEEE REW workshop paper: controlled experiment (N=60) on ChatGPT and undergraduates' fluency, originality, and flexibility, plus a perception survey (N=100); assignment method not stated.

CHI system paper (GraftMind): user study in which an AI mediator feeds collective ideas into private ideation workspaces, reporting better group ideation performance; comparison conditions, N, and assignment not in abstract, may be system_paper_no_comparison.
